prompt.brief: Design a like-counting system that keeps the actor-to-post relationship correct while serving accurate-enough counters and live updates for viral posts with millions of likes.
successSignals: Store one authoritative relationship per actor and post, then derive sharded counters and recent-liker views asynchronously.
Avoid a single hot post key by striped counters, partitioned event consumers, coalesced broadcasts, and bounded fanout.
Return the committed toggle immediately with a version and expose a count that may briefly lag under viral load.
Explain duplicate taps, unlike races, recount repair, privacy, moderation, abuse, and reconnect behavior.

functional: Like or unlike a post idempotently and return the actor's current state, count estimate, and monotonic version.
Display an accurate-enough count, recent eligible likers, and live deltas to connected viewers.
Support post deletion, blocked users, privacy rules, recounts, abuse limits, and durable audit events.
nonFunctional: Target p95 toggle acknowledgement below 150 ms and live counter propagation below 2 seconds for healthy rooms.
Handle viral posts with tens of millions of likes without synchronously incrementing one database row.
The relationship write must be durable and unique; counters and broadcasts may be eventually consistent.
Degrade to periodic refresh when live delivery or counter aggregation is behind, without losing toggles.
scaleAssumptions: Handle high-profile users with millions of likes
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Like-counting system commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Like-counting system writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Like-counting system version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Like-counting system by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Like-counting system work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Like-counting system projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Like-counting system projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Like-counting system records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Like-counting system latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines like idempotency, hot-post sharding, approximate counts, live updates, and recovery.
Entities and post/user/shard keys support unique likes, viral counters, privacy, live updates, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Like-counting system consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
